answer.policy_title: Medical Policy Manual – Surgery, Policy No. 228: Shoulder Surgeries
answer.effective_date: Effective December 1, 2025; Last Review October 2025; Next Review December 2026
criteria_quotes: II. Labral repair with or without capsulorrhaphy may be considered medically necessary when all of the following Criteria are met (A.-D.): A. Documentation of function-limiting pain (e.g., loss of shoulder function which interferes with the ability to carry out activities of daily living and/or demands of employment); and B. Either of the following criteria are met: 1. Failure to respond to at least three months of non-surgical management which includes documentation of physical therapy or prescribed home exercise program and one or more of the following unless contraindicated: a. Trial of anti-inflammatory medication; or b. Cortisone injection; or 2. The individual suffers from an acute traumatic dislocation with imaging documenting either acute capsule-labral separation or acute bony Bankart lesion and documented recurrent episodes of instability; and C. Advanced diagnostic imaging study (e.g., MRI, CT) demonstrates labral tear (e.g., SLAP, Bankart) and correlates with the individual's reported symptoms and physical exam findings; and D. All of the following are met (1. and 2.) based on physical examination when compared to the non-involved side: 1. Normal or minimally limited active or passive shoulder range of motion; and 2. One or more of the following positive orthopedic tests: a. O'Brien's Test; or b. Biceps Load Test; or c. Clunk Test; or d. Anterior Slide Test; or e. Compression Rotation Test; or f. Speed's Test; or g. Modified dynamic labral shear; or h. Apprehension test; or i. Anterior or posterior load and shift test; or j. Positive sulcus sign.
answer.appeal_deadline: 2027-02-18 (180 days from the August 22, 2026 notice date, as stated in the denial letter)
answer.submission_route: For BCBSNM group (employer-sponsored) plans: mail the Member/Provider Appeal form and supporting documents (denial letter, medical records) to BCBSNM Appeals Department, P.O. Box 660058, Dallas, TX 75266-0058; urgent appeals can be phoned to 866-236-1702 (TTY/TDD 711) or faxed to 918-551-2011. For BCBSNM Individual and Family (ACA marketplace) plans, mail to BCBSNM Claim Review Section, P.O. Box 660058, Dallas, TX 75266-0058; urgent requests can be phoned to 800-447-7828 (TTY/TDD 711) or faxed to 918-551-2011. Because the notice identifies this as a 'Commercial/ACA' plan, confirm with the number on the back of the member ID card which of these two appeal channels (group vs. individual/marketplace) applies, and use the correct phone/fax for urgent (expedited) appeals. A completed Member Appeal Form (or the 'Provider Request for Appeal on Behalf of Member' form if the surgeon is filing) should be included, along with the denial letter, clinical notes, imaging reports, exam findings, and documentation of conservative treatment addressing the criteria above.
answer.how_to_obtain_criteria: The criteria above were retrieved directly from BCBSNM's shared Health Care Service Corporation (HCSC) Medical Policy Manual, which is the same manual made available to members/providers through the official BCBSNM portal at medicalpolicy.bcbsnm.com (confirmed live and branded 'Blue Cross Blue Shield of New Mexico' when accessed with corpEntCd=NM). The underlying PDF documents in that manual are hosted on BCBS's document CDN (getbynder.com) rather than directly on bcbsnm.com. If you want BCBSNM to confirm in writing that SUR228 (or a specific sub-section) was the exact criteria applied to this denial, call the member services number on the back of the ID card or the number in the denial letter and request '(1) the specific medical policy number and version cited in this denial, and (2) a full copy of the clinical rationale/criteria used in the review,' which BCBSNM is required to provide upon request as part of the ACA appeal disclosure requirements.
answer.notes: CPT 29806 (arthroscopy, shoulder, surgical; capsulorrhaphy) corresponds most directly to Section II ('Labral repair with or without capsulorrhaphy') of SUR228. I could not pull the literal, final denial letter's citation of a specific policy number from the payer (the notice itself does not name one), so this identification rests on (a) confirming medicalpolicy.bcbsnm.com is BCBSNM's live, authoritative medical-policy portal, and (b) that portal serving the HCSC-wide Medical Policy Manual, of which 'Shoulder Surgeries, SUR228' is the document governing this CPT code family. I did not find a separate, NM-specific PDF hosted at bcbsnm.com naming SUR228 verbatim, so I recommend the patient/provider confirm the exact policy version cited in their file by contacting BCBSNM directly (see how_to_obtain_criteria) before finalizing the appeal, and attach the SUR228 criteria quoted above as the working basis for the appeal argument in the meantime. The appeal deadline and PO Box/phone numbers were confirmed directly from BCBSNM's own published provider/member appeal form.
